newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill 10 rebels in Casbah siege.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill 10 rebels in Casbah siege.

text.p: Algerian security forces backed by crack army troops killed at least 10 Moslem rebels in a 12 hour-siege of Algiers's Casbah, a rebel stronghold in the old centre of the Algerian capital, residents said on Sunday.
The security forces ringed the Casbah neighbourhood shortly after Moslem guerrillas shot dead three policemen in Algiers on Saturday and fled into the area's narrow streets.
"The siege started at about 11.30 a.m. (1030 GMT) on Saturday before being lifted at about midnight (2300 GMT)," said one resident.
The security forces closed off the area to stop civilians being caught in the crossfire, he said.
"Three rebels were killed in a first raid at 2.40 p.m. (1340 GMT on Saturday) while the seven others were shot dead in a second raid about five hours later," said another resident.
The authorities have made no comment on the violence.
The siege was the latest in a series of violent incidents in the capital over the last three years.
Last month security forces fired rockets into a Moslem guerrilla hideout, killing eight rebels. The authorities suspected them of killing Algeria's top union leader Abdelhk Benhamouda on January 28.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
